notes:
Summary of account / key constraints:
- Company: Cerberus builds real-time assistance and orchestration for autonomous fleets; inference decisions feed into low-latency vehicle control and operator dashboards.
- Primary ask: Dedicated GPU capacity across 3 regions with deterministic throughput guarantees + defined cross-region failover headroom.
- Latency SLOs: P95 target <40ms for short RPCs, P99 (tail) ≤100ms for end-to-end inference at <=512 tokens; CTO: "cannot accept >100ms tail latency for production driving assistance".
- Throughput baseline: projected steady-state 600 qps (combined fleet signals) with peaks up to 1.8k qps during regional events (map updates/overnight batch uploads). They want reserved capacity sized for baseline + 40% headroom per region, with cross-region failover capacity to cover a full-region outage (target: 1.5x baseline aggregated).
- Preferred hardware: H100-80GB (or A100-80GB fallback). Interested in quantized pipelines (FP16/INT8) for cost but require validated quality/regression tests.
- Pool topology ask: 3 primary regions (us-west2, us-east1, eu-west1), 2 AZs per region (spread for AZ-loss tolerance). Prefer even distribution but want ability to shift capacity quickly (autoscaling add-on for bursts).
- Failover policy: warm standby pools (0-5min ramp) + automatic routing; desire for hot-warm split so critical control paths have hot pool reserved, noncritical analytics use warm/burst. They require testable RTOs: regional failover RTO <5 minutes and per-AZ failover <90s for hot paths.
- Caching/consistency: KV-cache replication strategy for session affinity; ask: can Redwood replicate KV snapshots across regions or do we rely on prefix caching on-request? (SE to propose).
- SLA negotiation points: uptime 99.95% for dedicated pools, clear latency SLOs with credits for breaches, guaranteed reserved GPU availability during maintenance windows, 4-hour on-call escalation for infra incidents.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high; willing to sign multi-year reserved capacity if pricing and headroom math align — wants a modeled TCO comparing: reserved pools + burst credits vs pure autoscale on-demand.
- Security/compliance: VPC-only peering, SAML SSO, audit logs sent to their Splunk, KMS integration (HSM preferable), EU data residency for EU fleet data.
- POC results so far: baseline latency on H100 equiv meets P95 target at baseline loads; tail spikes observed during cold KV-cache misses and large batch reranking jobs. Action: tune prefix caching and short TTLs.
- Quote from Head of Infra: "We need deterministic unit economics before we commit — show us the math for reserved vs burst pricing and the worst-case failover cost".
- Sales motion: PLG -> AE driven: moving to procurement once SLA redlines and reserved counts are agreed.
POC milestones / asks outstanding:
- 1) Provide region-by-region reserved GPU proposal (counts per AZ) + explicit headroom math (Jordan/Priya)
- 2) Draft SLA redlines (trial credits for P99 breach) and fallback routing guarantees (SE + Legal)
- 3) Network peering workbook + latency expectations (customer infra team to sign)
- 4) On-prem packaging options & air-gapped checklist (R&D ask)
